title_clean: Greater Discourse to Sakuludāyī (MN 77) — The 37 Bodhipakkhiya Dhammā
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the 37 factors essential for liberation from the Mahā Sakuludāyī Sutta, connecting ancient wisdom to modern practice.
description_long:
In this illuminating talk, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Mahā Sakuludāyī Sutta (MN 77), focusing on the 37 Bodhipakkhiya Dhammā—the factors essential for full liberation. He addresses questions about the authenticity of Buddhist scriptures while emphasizing that the Dhamma is meant for investigation, not blind belief.

The talk systematically covers all 37 factors: the four satipaṭṭhāna (foundations of Right Awareness), the four sammappadhāna (great efforts), the four iddhipāda (bases of spiritual power), the five indriya (spiritual faculties), the five bala (powers), the seven bojjhaṅga (factors of awakening), and the Noble Eightfold Path. Bhante demonstrates how these ancient teachings apply not only to formal meditation but also to success in daily life activities.

Particularly valuable is his explanation of how spiritual faculties become powers upon attaining stream-entry, and his practical interpretation of concepts like chanda (wholesome desire) versus taṇhā (craving). The discourse concludes with the simple yet profound advice: maintain affectionate awareness and let unwholesome states pass naturally while cultivating right intention.
